marks.gloss_en: Pesach and sacrifices [which must be eaten] -- what is there to say? so even for R' Meir: where possible it is required, where impossible not
מה נפשך: if an agent is presumed to perform his agency, then teruma too [is presumed separated]; if he is not, then slaughter too [is not presumed done] -- either way the two rulings should agree
an agent is presumed to perform his agency

Rav Nachman: לכי תיכול עלה כורא דמילחא -- there is no presumption that an agent performs his agency; slaughter is presumed valid even if another heard and slaughtered, since most found at slaughter are experts, whereas teruma separated by another who heard is separated without the owner's knowledge and is not teruma
one who separates teruma without [the owner's] knowledge -- his teruma is not teruma
מי לא תניא: הרי שמצא תרנגולת שחוטה בשוק... חזקתו שחוט -- אלמא אמרינן רוב מצויין אצל שחיטה מומחין הן (kind svara under protest: no support kind for a rhetorical מי לא תניא)
the baraita: one who found a slaughtered chicken in the market, or told his agent 'go slaughter' and went and found it slaughtered -- its presumption is that it was [properly] slaughtered
קשיא דרבי אדרבי! -- on this account Rebbi's 'refuse heap' and 'house' both mean the heap in the house, so Rebbi sides with R' Yehuda and with R' Chanina in the same case
האמרת דכולי עלמא לא פליגי דשרי -- in an actual house all agree it is permitted
Rebbi's 'house' is an actual house
למה לי ראה? -- if he is known to be learned, why must he have seen?
פשיטא! -- if he is known not to be learned, that one must have seen the whole slaughter is obvious
proposed: the dictum speaks of one who knows the slaughterer is learned
לימא רוב מצויין אצל שחיטה מומחין הן -- מי לא תניא: one who found a slaughtered chicken in the market... חזקתו שחוט (p_baraita_matza_shachut); אלמא אמרינן רוב מצויין (p_rov_mumchin)
proposed: the dictum speaks of one who does not know whether the slaughterer is learned or not
לא, דכולי עלמא רוב מצויין אצל שחיטה מומחין הן -- all agree to the principle
[found] in a house -- all agree it is permitted
הא אמרת דכולי עלמא לא פליגי דאסור -- in the market heap all agree it is forbidden, so it would not be R' Yehuda's view alone
Rebbi's 'refuse heap' is the refuse heap in the market
one who saw a man slaughter: if he saw him from beginning to end, he may eat of his slaughter
most of those who are found at slaughter are experts
the dictum speaks of one who knows the slaughterer is not learned, and he cut one siman properly before us
one who told his agent 'go slaughter' and went and found it slaughtered -- its presumption is slaughtered
one whose kids and roosters were lost and who found them slaughtered -- R' Yehuda forbids [them]
proposed: they disagree over whether we say that most found at slaughter are experts
